title: Which sideband, and where it sits
idea: Below 10 MHz, voice is lower sideband; from 14 MHz up, upper sideband, by custom. The dial shows the suppressed carrier, and the 3 kHz signal sits on one side of it, so keep 3 kHz from the edge it grows toward.

rows: 3 kHz LSB near a lower edge
Carrier at least 3 kHz above it
3 kHz USB near an upper edge
Carrier at least 3 kHz below it

config.heading: Tune for the sideband
config.lead: Pick a band and a mode; the sideband follows the custom. Turn the dial near a band edge and watch the 3 kHz signal in the close-up.

compare.how: Occupies the 3 kHz below the displayed carrier.
Occupies the 3 kHz above the displayed carrier.
One sideband sent; the other sideband and the carrier suppressed.

traps.wrong: Lower sideband is the only sideband legal on these frequency bands
traps.why: Both are legal. LSB is just commonly accepted practice.

traps.wrong: Only one sideband and the carrier are transmitted; the other sideband is suppressed

traps.why: That's USB. LSB sits below the carrier: 7.175 to 7.178.

traps.wrong: At least 3 kHz below the edge of the segment
traps.why: Below the lower edge is outside the segment. LSB grows downward, so stay 3 kHz above it.
RTTY uses LSB; the JT and FT digital modes use USB.
